body: @gsoltis so it only happens when you call size() ?

So far, yes, that's the only place I've seen it. We have each event loop hooked up to a stats reporting module that reports the size of the task queue every few seconds. We noticed it because the stats stopped being reported, and it turns out the reporting thread was blocked on the call to `.size()`, which in turn was spinning on `peekNode()`. 

Here's the last few lines of the stacktrace:

> "StatsDLogger" prio=10 tid=0x00007f8e08f83800 nid=0x5664 runnable [0x00007f78f105b000]
>   java.lang.Thread.State: RUNNABLE
>   at io.netty.util.internal.MpscLinkedQueue.peekNode(MpscLinkedQueue.java:109)
>   at io.netty.util.internal.MpscLinkedQueue.size(MpscLinkedQueue.java:166)
>   at 
> io.netty.util.concurrent.SingleThreadEventExecutor.pendingTasks(SingleThreadEventExecutor.java:287)

it's not a lot to go on :)

@gsoltis what I can tell you is that size() is now allowed to be called by another thread then the EventLoop. Thinking about a proper fix.

issue.title: [#3675] Fix livelock issue in MpscLinkedQueue

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Motivation:

All read operations should be safe to execute from multiple threads which was not the case and so could produce a livelock.

Modifications:

Modify methods so these are safe to be called from multiple threads.

Result:

No more livelock.
